prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 141px · one-line width 141px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 129px · one-line width 1217px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 185px · one-line width 293px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 174px · one-line width 777px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 788px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 787px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A reference table for onboarding engineers and support staff to validate customer input fields: each row names a field, gives its regex rule, a valid sample, and the user-facing error text.","reading":"Readers scan row by row, using Field as the anchor, then inspect Pattern and check Example valid / Error message. Pattern is the longest technical content and will wrap regardless; error messages are prose and can wrap naturally; field names and sample values should remain recognizable tokens.","groups":["Field + Example valid: concrete input identity; keep adjacent so a reader can confirm what the field accepts.","Pattern + Error message: validation rule and its diagnostic; both explain why an input passes or fails."],"keep_intact":["Field identifiers such as account_email, phone_e164, postal_code_us","Regex unbreakable tokens and character classes, especially the longest ~129px token","Example valid values such as email addresses, phone numbers, dates, amounts, slugs and VAT IDs","Header words; avoid mid-word breaks"],"may_wrap":["Error message prose at word boundaries","Pattern at safe punctuation or group boundaries between intact regex tokens","Example valid only when unavoidable, preferably at natural separators"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [162, 195, 206, 224] · table 788×952px · row heights [39, 253, 118, 92, 93, 145, 118, 92] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [162, 204, 206, 215] · table 788×1005px · row heights [39, 253, 145, 92, 93, 145, 145, 92] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [162, 214, 206, 205] · table 788×1031px · row heights [39, 227, 171, 92, 93, 145, 145, 118] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
